audience.programmeDescription: Film and Literary Studies at Leiden examines how films and literary texts tell stories, create meaning and engage with society. Students practise close reading and film analysis, study historical movements and compare works across cultures and media. The programme offers Film Studies and Literary Studies tracks. This record follows Film Studies, including film theory, documentary, digital cinema and a research thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The supported components are shown below, but a complete degree pathway and UCR comparison remain unconfirmed. The allocation of the World Cinema courses and the applicable future sequence still need clarification. This uncertainty does not establish that UCR offers no meaningful study possibilities.

curriculum.limitation: The listed distinct components total 175 EC. One 5-EC World Cinema allocation still needs confirmation, and the placement of future courses must respect their entry requirements. This is an incomplete degree pathway.

componentNotes.y1-lit-theory: Introduces literary concepts, theory and interpretation in relation to other media.
componentNotes.y1-text-image-1: Develops detailed analysis of narrative form, perspective, characters, space and time in prose and film.
componentNotes.y1-text-image-2: Extends analysis to poetic language and non-narrative or non-mainstream cinema.
componentNotes.y1-world-cinema-b: World Cinema is counted once here. Confirmation of the separate A/B allocation is still needed before the second slot can be included.
componentNotes.y2-interculturality: Studies identity, difference and postcolonial approaches through cultural and literary objects.
componentNotes.y2-film-theory: Examines film-specific theoretical approaches, including semiotics, ideology and psychoanalysis.
componentNotes.y2-cinema-postmodern: Builds on introductory film analysis to study postmodern cinema, representation and complex narratives.
componentNotes.y2-paragone: Studies relations between words and images through theoretical texts, literature, film and visual art.
componentNotes.y2-documentary: Examines documentary representation in relation to evidence, truth, reality and ethics.
componentNotes.y3-film-philosophy: A 10-EC film-philosophy course requiring completion of a first-year Humanities programme.
componentNotes.y3-cinema-digital: Requires Realism and Modernism plus at least two of Postmodernism and Complex Narratives, Third Cinema, and Film and Philosophy to be completed beforehand.
componentNotes.thesis: A 10-EC research thesis of 10,000 words, normally in Dutch, with MLA conventions and two readers. Students must first earn at least 90 EC in Film and Literary Studies courses.
componentNotes.elective-space: 30 EC of genuine elective space for an approved package, minor, internship or study abroad. Future placement needs to fit the required course sequence; no particular elective subjects are assumed.
